etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English glotien / glotten, probably derived from Old French gloter / glotir / glotoiier (“to eat greedily”) [compare French engloutir (“to devour”), French glouton (“glutton”)], derived from Latin gluttiō, gluttīre (“to swallow”). Compare Russian глота́ть (glotátʹ, “to swallow”).
senses: (transitive) To fill to capacity; to satisfy all demand or requirement; to sate.
(transitive, economics) To provide (a market) with so much of a product that the supply greatly exceeds the demand.
